A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Spatial-DISE research work. All 33 pages in each version support comparison, including figures, tables, equations and appendices. Appendix pages 15-33 have identical text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v3 reports original VLM evaluations, supervised fine-tuning and transfer results, a human performance study, and error analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains the original VLM evaluations, fine-tuning and transfer results, human performance study, and error analyses, including their appendix results.

M1.justification: The benchmark curation procedure, five synthetic task-generation algorithms, and LoRA fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A.4 and B.4.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same ten Spatial-DISE tasks, four cognitive quadrants and 3D training coverage. External evaluation still uses CVBench, SAT, SPACE, OmniSpatial and VSIBench_MCQ.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same 32 evaluated VLMs, two DISE-fine-tuned variants, and human and random baselines. Table 3 preserves the same base-versus-SFT comparisons for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and SpaceOm.

E3.justification: Dataset splits in Table 7, exact-match evaluation and answer parsing in Section 4.1, human assessment design, prompting and decoding settings, and training hyperparameters in Table 14 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 3 retains the quadrant-transfer and 3D-to-2D analyses. Table 5 retains the merged-versus-separate-image ablation, while Section 5 and Appendix C preserve the same 200-error analysis and case studies.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same 95% confidence-interval reporting. Appendix B.1 preserves the CTT and IRT uncertainty-estimation procedures, with no additions or revisions to run-count or seed information.

E6.justification: Numerical results, transfer heatmaps and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains base/SFT accuracies of 26.1%/47.0% for Qwen2.5-VL-7B and 25.9%/41.3% for SpaceOm.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 retains the same CTT expressions, two-parameter logistic IRT model and uncertainty formulas in Equations 1-8. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a cognitively grounded benchmark, scalable verifiable data generation, and evidence of a persistent VLM-human spatial-reasoning gap.

C2.justification: Interpretations of mental-simulation failures, selective transfer and perceptual confounders are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations concerning judge bias, the small error sample, sim-to-real transfer and partial manual verification.

D1.justification: Generation pseudocode, software and hardware details, evaluation prompts, API checkpoints and SFT hyperparameters are unchanged. Benchmark, dataset and code access statements are also retained.

R1.justification: Section 2, Table 1 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and research positioning. Reference pagination changes without additions or removals of prior work.

P1.justification: v4 adds a funding acknowledgment footnote and author marker, changes 'Corresponding author' to 'Corresponding authors', and lightly edits Table 2's caption. Scientific prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added footnote reflows the main text, splitting the abstract across pages 1-2. Table 2 occupies page 7 alone, and Figure 3 moves from page 8 to page 9. Displays retain their content and structure; appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 adds funding disclosure and slight caption polish while retaining all scientific evidence, interpretations, limitations and reproducibility information. The associated reflow, including the split abstract, has modest presentation effects without meaningfully improving or weakening overall paper quality.
